nodes.claim: The perfect test axiom is one joint latent model over all instruments — the four core tests, the nine lenses and logic — not a shelf of separate scores.
nodes.detail: Raised conjecture→argued 2026-09-01: the node's own named test — show a concrete consumer that gets a different answer from the joint model than from the shelf — is now run against the product's shipped code rather than a hypothetical (src/v2/data/similarity.ts on main, read this run), with the adversarial pass's corrections applied and the seed draft's two failed shortcuts recorded here rather than papered over. THE CONSUMER. The Kindred/similarity field (D112/D277) is a shelf consumer in its primary tier: flattenAxes() flattens each instrument's axis scores into 'test:dim' keys — 22 axes over the four instruments, exactly 5 items per axis in the sit-down bank, and as few as 2 where the passive fold publishes (MIN_AXIS_ITEMS = 2) — and rankKindred prints 100 minus the mean absolute gap across shared axes (match) while ranking on the prior-shrunk version of the same quantity (raw; the D277 split). Logic is excluded from the distance by design (a verified score, D57, not an axis profile), and a second tier ranks score-less candidates by item-level answer agreement, which is not shelf arithmetic. WHERE INDEPENDENCE IS ASSUMED — corrected by this run's adversarial pass from the seed draft's claim of two sites: TYPICAL_AXIS_GAP (the shipped 17, derived from the closed form E|X−Y| = 15·√2·√(2/π) ≈ 16.93) assumes independence BETWEEN THE TWO PEOPLE on one axis — a marginal expectation, invariant to cross-axis correlation — so it is not an axis-independence assumption at all. The real one sits in the λ=6 calibration: the spread simulation that chose AXIS_PRIOR drew its 200 zero-similarity candidates with axes drawn N(50,15) independently across axes, so cross-axis correlation would change the width-dependent spread λ=6 was tuned to flatten. One load-bearing site, not two. THE ARGUMENT — this lane's own, held at argued: the equal-weight metric weights each latent dimension in proportion to how many observed axes load on it (a factor carried by k of p axes gets weight k/p), where an equal-weight-per-latent-dimension joint metric gives every factor the same weight. This is a RELATIVE re-weighting, not the k-fold amplification the seed draft claimed: the mean cancels the amplification exactly in the one-factor limit (two axes at r=1 give shelf distance |Δf| and joint distance |Δf| — identical rankings at maximal correlation), the re-weighting vanishes when loadings are uniform across factors, and axis-level uniqueness at 5 items per axis compresses it further (co-loading noisy axes dampen the shared component's marginal influence). What survives is enough to answer the test: wherever factors are UNEVENLY represented across the 22 axes, the shelf's implicit weights (axis counts) and the joint metric's weights differ and rankings flip — worked example in the adversarial record: axes A1=A2 on factor f, A3 on factor s; candidate A at |Δf|=3, |Δs|=0 vs candidate B at |Δf|=0, |Δs|=5 — shelf means 2.00 vs 1.67 rank B closer, equal-weight joint distances 1.50 vs 2.50 rank A closer. And the joint side's metric is itself a named choice, not geometry: a variance-weighted latent metric would move the weights the other way — the point is that the perfect axiom chooses its metric on purpose where the shelf chooses it by accident of how many axes each factor happens to load. Literature status, stated precisely (narrowed from the seed draft's over-claim): that equal-weight distance over correlated coordinates over-weights redundant directions, with Mahalanobis distance as the correction, is textbook multivariate statistics for squared distance; what this run found no source stating is the mean-absolute-gap, psychometric-axis-profile, ranking-consequence version — that composition is this lane's own, on tst-9's facts, of which Cronbach–Gleser (similarity indices are decomposition-sensitive) is the one genuinely in this register; Moshagen's sign-reversal is a measurement-model-choice result about covariate correlations, adjacent, cited as analogy only. THE HINGE, single and named: whether InSight's own 22 axes are correlated enough for any of this to bite is unmeasured, and near-zero local correlations would defeat BOTH consumers here — the ranking argument AND the precision argument, whose entire mechanism is the correlations (Wang's gain is zero at zero correlation; de la Torre & Patz's efficiency is 'most pronounced for highly correlated abilities'). The 2026-09-01 REQUESTS row is the single hinge for this node's route upward, not — as the seed draft had it — a hinge for half of it. THE PRECISION CONSUMER, with the transfer caveat: Wang, Chen & Cheng's less-than-half-the-items result holds under that study's simulated battery conditions (test length, number of tests, inter-trait correlation magnitude, ability-style items); it does not transfer as a constant to 5-item self-report axes. What transfers is the direction and the regime: the gain is largest exactly where this axiom lives — short tests, many of them, correlated — and at 5 items per axis (2 in the passive fold) per-axis precision is poor, so joint scoring is the largest precision lever the cited literature quantifies for this shape, with tst-2's passive administration and tst-4's per-era cadence making items-per-reading scarcer still. A new lens as a new set of loadings is de la Torre & Patz's short-correlated-tests case exactly: it borrows the joint prior instead of opening a silo from zero. COMMUNALITY, honestly scoped: tst-9's cited communality covers ability, personality and interest measures; nothing in the cited list covers politics, values or attachment inter-correlations, and logic — the one ability member of this battery — is excluded from this very metric. For THIS battery the correlation premise is analogical until measured; the REQUESTS row is again the route. THE DESIGN TENSION, corrected from the seed draft's over-read: D277 did NOT license printing one number while ranking on a different metric — it split match from raw while PRESERVING rank-monotonicity in the printed number (its own docblock: the prior cannot invert the metric at equal width; its pinned tests hold strict monotonicity across every width), a correction to the plan rather than the plan. A joint-model metric breaks that invariant — it would rank a printed 84 above a printed 91. So the perfect form BREAKS the D277 precedent rather than extending it, and this lane argues the break while recording it open: the invariant protects the explainability of a number that is itself the artifact under correlated axes ('100 minus the average gap' explains a distortion fluently), and the honest pair is a printed sentence about the joint reading plus a ranking consistent with it — but that is an argument, not a settlement, and it sits in Open problems. THE PUBLICATION BOUNDARY (tst-6/tst-7 reconciliation, added on the adversarial pass's finding): a person-to-person ranking is a per-person published output over latent estimates that tst-7 says are indeterminate — a 'joint-model ranking' is a family of orders, one per scoring method — and tst-6 settles publication to the model plus population-level sufficient statistics, never per-person latent draws. The perfect form's ranking must therefore carry the indeterminacy through the model — plausible-value-averaged ranks with their rank uncertainty, publishing the order and its stability, never latent coordinates — and whether an order over named people respects tst-6's publication boundary at all is recorded as an open problem, not assumed away. BOUNDS. 'One model' means one hierarchical model per tst-6's fork — between-person geometry and within-person state spaces, linked, never conflated; tst-3's two item families remain per-family link functions into the shared space; identity with the combination space is embedding, not exhaustion (tst-6). To cited: a source stating the mean-absolute profile-ranking version cleanly, or InSight's own correlation structure via the REQUESTS row — which diagnoses the OBSERVED shelf, not the latent couplings tst-6 reserves for the joint model, so consuming it raises this node without publishing a coupling. To measured: fit the joint model on InSight's data and compare rank stability both ways under plausible-value draws.

nodes.claim: Passive administration — instruments filled by ordinary answering in the flow of life, on state-worded items — is a measurement-theoretically distinct administration, not a budget compromise: in-the-moment items minimize the recall bias global self-report carries, their aggregates are trait-stable, and the within-person spread they alone can see is a stable individual difference.
nodes.detail: Raised argued→cited 2026-08-27; the seed's scout task — which of these claims the ambulatory-assessment literature supports — is answered, and the answer both grounds the node and adds a condition the seed missed. The cited premises: (i) global retrospective self-report is limited by recall bias, and collecting reports on current behavior and experience in the moment, in the person's natural environment, minimizes it while maximizing ecological validity — the defining rationale of ecological momentary assessment and ambulatory assessment (Shiffman–Stone–Hufford 2008; Trull & Ebner-Priemer 2013). (ii) Any single occasion is a poor measure of anything trait-like, and stability arrives through aggregation: averaging over increasing numbers of events raises stability coefficients to high levels across objective behavior, self-ratings and others' ratings (Epstein 1979). (iii) Momentary states vary so widely that the typical person routinely manifests nearly all levels of all traits in ordinary weeks, yet each person's density distribution of states is stable — its central tendency almost perfectly, and its variability, skew and kurtosis as stable individual differences in their own right (Fleeson 2001); and global Big Five scores predict the CENTRE of those distributions well, while their associations with variability, skew and kurtosis largely vanish once the mean and squared mean are controlled, the maximum excepted (Fleeson & Gallagher 2009) — which is exactly why the spread is not recoverable from a sit-down score. THE CONDITION (this run's adversarial pass, made load-bearing rather than hedged): the EMA advantage attaches to the item's REFERENT, not to the answering context. The sources' mechanism is momentary state reports; a global dispositional item ('I keep appointments and rarely run late') answered in a feed is still a global retrospective self-report — it inherits none of (i), and its repeats measure retest variance on a disposition rating rather than (iii)'s state distribution. InSight's current instrument items are global-dispositional (content/tests.json), so D121's passive fold is the delivery half of the perfect form's shadow only; the perfect form re-words instrument items from global-dispositional to momentary-state and lets aggregation (ii) rebuild the trait from states. What stays ARGUED rather than cited, plainly: any superiority claim. None of these sources runs the head-to-head — an EMA-aggregated battery against a single-sitting battery on criterion validity — and the counter-evidence sits inside this very source list: Fleeson & Gallagher show a single-sitting Big Five already predicts the distribution's centre well, so passive administration's incremental value is concentrated in the spread and the trajectory (tst-4), not the mean — which is where a superiority claim must eventually be tested. Per-item reliability in the wild is LOWER (Epstein's curve read from the other end), so the design owes the aggregation it depends on; 'test-taking mode' as a validity threat is likewise still argument here — que-2's response-process frame is where it becomes estimable, and re-served items owe que-2's calibration for retest effects. Verification note: publisher full-text egress-blocked from this container; sources corroborated at search-index/metadata level against at least two independent records each (the questions/body lanes' precedent), and independently re-verified by this run's adversarial pass.

nodes.claim: Ability and disposition need different measurement theory, and the perfect axiom holds both in one space without conflating them.
nodes.detail: Logic is scored against a key (there IS a right answer; guessing and ceiling effects matter); the instruments are self-positioning (there is no right answer; social desirability and reference-group effects matter). The perfect joint model (tst-1) therefore has two item families with different link functions, sharing one person-space. Treating logic as 'just another instrument' or the instruments as 'soft ability' are the two symmetric mistakes.

nodes.claim: In the perfect axiom a test result is a trajectory, not a number.
nodes.detail: Create-once scoring converges and freezes; people do not. The perfect axiom re-measures on a cadence (fresh item instances per era, the pulse move applied to instruments) and reports change with its uncertainty — 'has your openness moved' as a first-class reading. Depends on bod-5's within-person frame and que-2's item parameters (an item re-served must be calibrated for retest effects). Edge fix 2026-08-29: the bod-5 edge was typed supports while this detail said depends since creation — flagged by the 2026-08-27 adversarial pass, corrected by this lane (its own node) rather than left to the optimizer. The dependency is on bod-5's within-person design-grain argument, which survives bod-5's own 2026-08-29 re-scope (the sleep-only clause it was narrowed to concerns the within-vs-between ORDERING, which tst-4 does not lean on).

nodes.claim: Personality's normal-range latent structure is predominantly dimensional rather than taxonic, so any archetype can only be a density region of continuous trait space with a drawn boundary — and the region solutions the literature reports are real but sample-, method- and preprocessing-fragile.
nodes.detail: Raised conjecture→cited 2026-08-29, and FISSIONED the same run on the adversarial pass's finding: the seed claim mixed this evidence with design composition under one status, against this lane's own tst-2 precedent (only cited material in a cited claim string), so the evidence lives here and the design composition — between-person placement, versioned re-anchoring, similarity-to-region reporting, human-authored naming — is tst-8 (argued). FACT ONE — TAXA ARE POORLY SUPPORTED AS THE DEFAULT. Haslam, Holland & Kuppens' quantitative review of taxometric research (177 articles, 311 distinct findings, combined N=533,377 — spanning personality AND psychopathology, so the aggregate figures are cross-domain, the personality-specific breakdown not being established at the verification grade available this run) found 38.9% of findings taxonic on their face, but taxonic findings were much less frequent in more recent and methodologically stronger studies, and with confounds statistically controlled the estimated true prevalence falls to about 14% — with normal-range personality specifically among the domains yielding little support for categorical models. McCrae & Costa found, for the canonical authored type system, no support for the view that the MBTI measures truly dichotomous preferences or qualitatively distinct types: the instrument measures four relatively independent continuous dimensions, which track aspects of four of the five major dimensions of normal personality (the Judging–Perceiving index itself flagged by the authors as questionable) — a 1989 volunteer sample of 468, a historical anchor rather than load-bearing structural evidence. So a discrete-kind reading of normal-range types is poorly supported as the default; a type, where one is drawn, is a REGION, and every boundary is drawn, not discovered — which converts the boundary from an empirical claim into a design responsibility (honesty about arbitrariness at the edges; distance-to-boundary is publishable where a hard label would lie). FACT TWO — REGIONS ARE REAL BUT FRAGILE, AND THE FRAGILITY IS DOCUMENTED ON BOTH SIDES. Data-anchoring is possible: Gerlach, Farb, Revelle & Nunes Amaral, clustering Big Five data from four large (self-selected online) samples totalling more than 1.5 million respondents — motivated, in the abstract's own words, by the prior literature's lack of reproducibility across data sets and methods — report robust evidence for AT LEAST four distinct personality types; the resilient/overcontrolled/undercontrolled prototypes replicate across children and adults, in both replicated cluster analyses and replicated Q-factor analyses (Asendorpf, Borkenau, Ostendorf & Van Aken — an affirmative confirmation paper, cited for that replication finding); and across 40 years, bootstrapped internal replication supports a tripartite ARC structure that is 'fuzzy rather than discrete', best represented as gradients of similarity to three prototype Big Five profiles (Chapman & Goldberg) — the cleanest empirical statement that concentrations can be real, even predictive, and are gradients in a continuous space rather than partitions. The instability: in 1,540 California Adult Q-Set self-sorts, none of the person-factors reported in the prior literature replicated across random subsamples; the two factors that did replicate were artifacts of mean-level endorsement differences, at least three replicable factors emerged only after item standardization, and five extracted person-factors then aligned with the five-factor dimensions (McCrae, Terracciano, Costa & Ozer) — instability plus method- and preprocessing-dependence in one study, with the dimensions as what survives; and Freudenstein, Strauch, Mussel & Ziegler's published Matters Arising reanalysis of Gerlach's Johnson-300 data concurs four meaningful clusters exist but finds only ~42% of the sample associated with them — the majority of people fall in no distinct cluster — while Gerlach, Revelle & Nunes Amaral's Reply maintains the computational findings and shares the concern about premature assessment use. STATED AS CONTRARY, NOT ABSORBED: McCrae et al. 2006 and Freudenstein's 42% are evidence AGAINST deriving stable person-regions from population structure at all, not merely counsel for careful anchoring — this node's fragility clause records that tension rather than resolving it, and region-anchoring survives only as a TESTABLE design commitment (tst-8's second clause; this run's REQUESTS row is its local test). The traditions also disagree with each other — three Q-sort prototypes versus at least four density clusters — and that disagreement is itself part of the fragility record. Honesty notes on attribution: 'density regions, not discrete taxa' is this node's operationalization-level reading (plus the critics' 42% finding), not Gerlach et al.'s own framing, which speaks of distinct types and floated assessment utility; Freudenstein's robustness prong is characterized here only by its title and verified exhaustiveness finding, the specific non-robust analyses being unverifiable at metadata level. Verification note: publisher full-text egress-blocked from this container; every source corroborated at search-index/metadata level against at least two independent records by a dedicated verification pass this run, which supplied the numeric figures and quoted findings above (all specifics in this detail are from that pass, none from memory); single-sourced residue named plainly: Asendorpf's issue number (3) was corroborated by one indexed record only.

nodes.claim: The perfect archetype system is a design composition over tst-5's facts: regions anchored in the between-person geometry, re-anchored only as deliberate versioned events, reported as similarity-to-region rather than forced nearest-type labels, with names human-authored.
nodes.detail: Split out of tst-5 on 2026-08-29's adversarial finding (design clauses may not ride a cited badge; the tst-2 precedent). Types earn their keep as compression for humans — a region-name beats five numbers in conversation — and each clause is this lane's argument on cited scaffolding, none itself cited. PLACEMENT (answers central's 2026-08-28 follow-up b): types live in the between-person geometry. The anchor coordinate is the person's density-distribution central tendency — Fleeson's near-perfectly stable parameter (cited at tst-2), with the honest hedge that Fleeson's stability is across occasions within experience-sampling windows, while a type-name's promise is longitudinal over years; the longer horizon is an assumption tst-4's trajectories exist to test, not a cited fact. A type read off momentary states would churn daily — the stability a type-name promises is available only from the between-person coordinate. This does not exile the within-person geometry from typing: Fleeson's spread parameters are themselves stable individual differences, i.e. legitimate between-person COORDINATES derived from within-person data — so the region-space may include spread dimensions (a 'steady/volatile' cut), but the region-space itself remains a between-person object. RE-ANCHORING: because tst-5 shows region solutions are sample-, method- and preprocessing-sensitive, region anchors must be versioned artifacts changed only by announced re-anchoring, never as a side effect of a fit re-running; a person's type may move only when their own aggregated position moves (tst-4's trajectory, with uncertainty) or when an anchoring version changes visibly. REPORTING: Freudenstein's 42% plus Chapman & Goldberg's gradients (via tst-5) say the perfect system reports similarity-to-region rather than forcing every person into a nearest region — 'no distinct type; nearest is X at distance d' is a legal, honest reading, and under tst-5's contrary evidence it may be the majority reading. NAMING: human-authored — a warmth act, not an optimization; pure design claim, offered without evidence and marked so. CONTRAST WITH SHIPPED: archetype-data.js on main is authored signature vectors with hand-written shares and nearest-type matching — the authored-grid form this composition replaces; whether InSight's own population shows density structure near those signatures is what this run's REQUESTS row would make measurable, and it is also the test that could DEFEAT the first clause (tst-5's contrary evidence predicts most people may sit in no distinct region).

nodes.claim: The tests space embeds in the combination space rather than being identical to it; what identity holds, holds at the level of the latent model, never a published score table; and the joint model is hierarchical — between-person structure does not carry within-person couplings, so cen-1's one coordinate system is two linked geometries.
nodes.detail: Answers central's 2026-08-26 question (this lane's QUESTIONS.md) — cen-1 assumed the instrument space and the cross-axiom combination space are one object and invited a counterargument; the answer is a partial fork in three parts, ordered from what survives to what does not. It stands on tst-7's grounded facts and is held at ARGUED per the questions lane's que-5/que-6 precedent: the facts are cited, but their composition into an architecture claim is this lane's own argument, and §4 says the status stays down. (1) EMBEDDING, NOT EXHAUSTION. One instrument-grade model can carry the four instruments, the nine lenses and logic — mixed multidimensional models with a link function per item family over one shared person space are standard machinery, and tst-3's two families are exactly a per-family link choice (que-2's Birnbaum/Samejima frame, widened). But what the test items span is a SUBSPACE of the combination space: other axioms measure dimensions on which every test item loads near zero (bod-6's regulatory-system parameters; cen-3's chronotype candidates), and those coordinates are identified by THOSE axioms' measurement models, not by the instrument. Identifying the combination space with the tests audit layer strictly would either project such dimensions onto instrument-space — loss wearing measurement's clothes — or append coordinates the instrument never identifies, at which point the object is cen-1's joint model rather than the tests instrument. An embedding is precisely not an identity: the tests space is a sub-coordinate-system of the joint space, and que-5 makes the same point from the bank's side. (2) MODEL, NOT SCORE TABLE. Where identity holds, it holds at the level of the latent model, never of a published table of person point-scores: tst-7's second fact (factor-score indeterminacy; the plausible-values remedy) means couplings must be computed through the joint model, never as correlations between columns of point scores — otherwise pat-5's honesty failures are baked into the publication format itself, and pat-2's recompute contract reproduces the artifact faithfully: recomputability guarantees only faithful reproduction of whatever the published form contains. The §9 boundary settles the publication form: what is published is the model plus POPULATION-LEVEL sufficient statistics that reproduce the couplings with their uncertainty (e.g. moment matrices over plausible-value draws, aggregated), never per-person latent draws — §9 forecloses person-level publication of latent estimates, and pat-2's reader-recomputability is satisfied by the aggregate form. (3) THE FORK — BETWEEN IS NOT WITHIN. cen-1's 2026-08-26 form (and pat-3's 2026-08-25 form, since rewritten to agree) implied that within-person couplings (bod-5's frame; tst-4's trajectories) are geometry in the same shared space, and that is the part that did not survive tst-7's first fact: between-person structure generalizes within persons only under rarely-met ergodicity conditions, and within-person variance runs two to four times larger than group-level estimates even where central tendencies show some agreement — means may travel between the two levels; spreads and structure do not. So an audit layer fitted on between-person covariance cannot double as the coordinate system for within-person change: 'has your openness moved' answered by tracking a between-person coordinate silently assumes the cross-level loading invariance that must instead be tested. What this forks in cen-1 is the singular: 'one joint person-model … one published coordinate system' is really TWO linked published geometries — a between-person coordinate system (cen-1's audit layer, intact) and within-person state spaces with their own estimated loadings, joined in one hierarchical model — or it claims ergodicity without saying so. Hence the original 2026-08-27 edge pair to cen-1: refines for the whole, contradicts scoped to that one component, so the optimizer's health summary would surface the open fork — see the RESOLUTION below for what became of each. To measured: fit within-person loadings on InSight's own repeated measurements and test them against the published between-person loadings — which requires repeated instrument measurements that current serving policy does not produce (D5 is one-answer-per-item; D86 edits overwrite): this run's second REQUESTS row names era-scoped re-serving as the bridge decision that would create the data, and the pulse roster as the only shipped surface with true repeats today. RESOLUTION 2026-08-29 (answers central's 2026-08-28 follow-up a), accounting for BOTH original cen-1 edges: the contradicts edge, scoped to a claim string that no longer exists, is retired — cen-1 was revised 2026-08-28 to the hierarchical two-geometry form, the fork adopted wholesale (this run re-read the revised cen-1 clause by clause and found no component still in conflict). Central offered two options — retype contradicts→refines, or re-scope the contradiction — and this lane took a third, stated plainly: go-6's rule offers refines when the target has merely narrowed, but cen-1 did more than narrow — it adopted the fork's architecture and now carries a depends edge back to this node — so a supports edge is added: tst-6 is argument FOR the revised cen-1. The refines edge is KEPT alongside it, not silently dropped: the embedding-not-exhaustion bound lives in cen-1's detail but not in its claim string, so tst-6 still sharpens what cen-1 asserts. The program's first contradicts edge is thereby resolved by target revision, with this paragraph and the LOG row as the trace go-6 asks for — the health summary's contradiction count returning to zero reads as a closed work item rather than recording failure. The residual tension the resolution does NOT close: tst-5's contrary evidence on person-regions (McCrae et al. 2006; Freudenstein's 42%) is a live open question for the archetype layer, recorded at tst-5/tst-8, not here.

nodes.claim: Two grounded facts bound any joint person-model: between-person structure generalizes to within-person structure only under rarely-met ergodicity conditions, and person-level latent scores are indeterminate estimates that secondary analysis cannot consume directly — plausible values are the remedy.
nodes.detail: Added 2026-08-27 as the grounded scaffolding under tst-6, per the questions lane's que-5/que-6 precedent (the architecture conclusion stays argued; the facts it composes are cited). FACT ONE — LEVELS. Results from inter-individual variation generalize to intra-individual variation only under strict ergodicity conditions rarely met by real psychological processes (Molenaar 2004); empirically, across six repeated-measures datasets, within-person variance was two to four times larger than the group-level estimate even where central tendencies showed some agreement (Fisher–Medaglia–Jeronimus 2018) — means may agree across levels while spreads diverge. The modeling form: multilevel covariance structure analysis decomposes covariance into within- and between-cluster structure and models them separately (Muthén 1994) — with occasions-nested-in-persons as the nesting this lane needs, a case the framework covers though the paper's own illustration is group-clustered data — and within-person and between-person effects are distinct estimands a longitudinal model must disaggregate (Curran & Bauer 2011). FACT TWO — SCORES. Factor scores are indeterminate — the common-factor model does not fix them uniquely, scoring methods genuinely differ, and unexamined score estimates carried into later analyses are the named hazard (Grice 2001); population statistics over latent variables are exactly where standard secondary-analysis procedures on point estimates stop applying, and the plausible-values remedy — multiple imputation of the latent variable, with variance terms carrying both sampling and latency uncertainty — is the basis of NAEP-style practice (Mislevy 1991; Mislevy–Beaton–Kaplan–Sheehan 1992). Verification note: publisher full-text egress-blocked from this container; every source corroborated at search-index/metadata level against at least two independent records (the questions/body lanes' precedent), mapped claims kept to what those records carry, and the full set independently re-verified by this run's adversarial pass (12/12 across the run exact; zero invented).

nodes.claim: Separate per-scale scoring and joint scoring of correlated instruments are not interchangeable: multidimensional IRT scoring that exploits cross-trait correlations is substantially more precise than one-test-at-a-time scoring, how much reliable variance subscale scores carry beyond a general factor is an estimable question scoring must answer, the choice of structural model for hierarchical constructs changes downstream estimates even in sign, profile-similarity indices are decomposition-sensitive, and ability, personality and interest measures show cross-domain communality that is patterned — concentrated in trait complexes — not uniform.
nodes.detail: Added 2026-09-01 as the grounded scaffolding under tst-1, per this lane's established pattern (tst-7 under tst-6; the que-5/que-6 precedent): the facts are cited here; their composition into 'the perfect axiom is one joint model' stays tst-1's own argument, below cited. FACT ONE — BORROWING STRENGTH, QUANTIFIED. Scoring a battery one test at a time ignores the correlations between latent traits and yields imprecise measures when tests are short; multidimensional item response models use those correlations to improve measurement precision of individual latent traits, substantially so when tests are short and the number of tests is large — and to achieve the same measurement precision, the multidimensional approach needs less than half of the comparable items the unidimensional approach requires (Wang, Chen & Cheng 2004; abstract-grade, the quantified clause near-verbatim from the indexed record — and scoped honestly: that figure holds under the study's own simulated battery conditions of test length, battery size and inter-trait correlation magnitude, and is not a constant that transfers to an arbitrary battery; what transfers is the direction and the short-correlated-tests regime). Applied to real operational test data: simultaneously estimating correlated abilities in a hierarchical Bayesian framework yields more precise estimates per dimension, the efficiency most pronounced for highly correlated abilities estimated from multiple short tests (de la Torre & Patz 2005; no quantified gain is visible at this run's verification grade, so none is claimed for it). FACT TWO — SUBSCALE SCORES OWE A GENERAL-FACTOR ACCOUNTING. Showing item responses to be multifactorial does not by itself justify creating and scoring subscales; the fine-grained psychometric questions that settle scoring include to what degree total scale scores reflect reliable variation on a single construct, whether subscale reporting is justified, and how much reliable variance subscale scores provide after controlling for a general factor (Reise, Bonifay & Haviland 2013; abstract-grade near-verbatim). For hierarchically structured constructs, the alternative structural models — one-factor, first-order, higher-order, nested/bifactor — differ in model-based score reliabilities and in which research and diagnostic purposes each serves (Brunner, Nagy & Wilhelm 2012). FACT THREE — MODEL CHOICE CHANGES THE DOWNSTREAM ANSWER, UP TO ITS SIGN. How a hierarchically structured construct is modeled (higher-order vs bifactor vs single-factor over items vs single-factor over parcels) changes the estimated correlation between the general construct and covariates, up to turning a truly positive correlation negative (Moshagen 2023; the sign-reversal finding is carried by the verified title itself; cited without pagination — DOI/landing-page verification only). FACT FOUR — SIMILARITY INDICES ARE DECOMPOSITION-SENSITIVE. Profile similarity decomposes into elevation, scatter and shape; distance-type and correlation-type measures answer different questions; and reducing a configuration to a single index loses information the analyst must account for (Cronbach & Gleser 1953). FACT FIVE — THE INSTRUMENT FAMILIES CORRELATE. An extensive meta-analysis of personality–intellectual-ability correlations plus a review of interest–ability associations finds communality across the three domains, organized as four trait complexes: social, clerical/conventional, science/math, intellectual/cultural (Ackerman & Heggestad 1997). Deliberately NOT cited, named plainly: the specific meta-analytic r values commonly quoted from that paper (openness–g and kin) are table-level content unverifiable at this run's verification grade, so they stay out; and the four-complex structure means the overlap is patterned — concentrated in complexes — not uniform across all pairs, a hedge any consumer of this fact inherits. Kept OUT of this node, with the literature status stated precisely (the adversarial pass corrected the seed draft's broader 'no source states it'): that equal-weight distance over correlated coordinates over-weights redundant directions, with Mahalanobis distance as the correction, is textbook multivariate statistics for SQUARED distance; what this run found no source stating is the mean-absolute-gap, psychometric-axis-profile, ranking-consequence version tst-1 needs — that composition lives at tst-1 as this lane's own argument, below cited. EDGES, each a claim (SCHEMA): supports tst-1 — every fact above is scaffolding under its composition; supports tst-3 — fact five's cross-domain communality is evidence that the ability and disposition families belong in one person-space even as tst-3 keeps their link functions apart; supports tst-6 — fact three is estimator-level evidence for tst-6's 'couplings through the model, never score columns': when model choice can reverse a downstream correlation's sign, a published coupling cannot be model-free. Verification note: publisher full-text AND metadata-API egress fully blocked from this container; every source corroborated at search-index level against at least two independent DOI-bearing records by a dedicated verification pass this run, which corrected the seed list before writing (Wang et al.'s title says 'models' not 'theory'; the subscale-confounding claim moved off Reise 2012 — dropped entirely for claim mismatch and a possible unresolved erratum — onto Reise–Bonifay–Haviland 2013; Ackerman–Heggestad's r values excluded). All specifics above are from that pass, none from memory. Weakest fields are pagination and issue numbers, per that pass: Wang et al.'s end page and Cronbach & Gleser's issue number rest on repeated index listings rather than a fetched publisher record (the issue number is therefore omitted from that reference), and Moshagen's pagination is omitted here — the article has page numbers, but they were unverifiable at this run's grade, so they are not stated.
